call_points.text: Closing order book ₹5,143 Cr at end-Q1FY27, plus ₹800 Cr of orders received on the call day.
Fuel cell expansion in three phases: Phase 1 commissioned, Phase 2 by September-October, Phase 3 by March 2027.
Nuclear: ₹684 Cr of orders today, about ₹130 Cr more expected this quarter, execution starting H2FY27 over about three years.
Data centre infrastructure: about ₹45 Cr order to execute by February-March, with a potential requirement of eight such sets a year.
Aerospace and defence revenue expected to double this fiscal year, with a 3-4 year ramp from that base.
Longer-term ambition: products business above ₹1,000 Cr and aerospace ₹600-700 Cr, without a stated date.
Asked about interest cost split, the MD said he did not have the break-up and deferred to the CFO.
On US data centre capex delay concerns, management dismissed them as "unwanted noise" without giving numbers.
Phase 3 fuel cell capacity size was not disclosed, citing an NDA with the customer.
FY27 revenue growth guidance raised to 80% plus/minus 5% from 50%, with EBITDA margin around 24%.
Management expects closing order book near ₹5,000 Cr by end-FY27.
Capex of ₹250-300 Cr over two years for capacity expansion; initial clean energy capacity already commissioned.
Oil and gas plant to be commissioned by September end and fully operational.
First article export orders of ₹35 Cr for AI data centre assemblies; potential ₹400-500 Cr over next couple of years.
FY26 gross margin 47.7% versus 49.4% last year, impacted by higher consumable input prices and freight costs.
Fluence project dropped as customer deliberates on battery duties; prototypes done and door remains open.
